routes.app.request: Q1 `app.request`: invoke this pinned app-server client request on the session's own app-server connection. `class` is the required capability; `contexts` limits where it may be called (`user` = a user-invoked command, key or component action; `event` = lifecycle or notification handlers); `confirm` requires a native confirmation naming the mod; `scope` binds thread arguments to threads the caller may see; `refuse` lists parameters a mod may not set; `root` parameters must name the session root or one of its worktrees; `route_fields` must match a configured route; `keys` names the config keys the call writes, checked against `authority_config`.
routes.app.notification: Q1 `app_notification` event: observe this server notification through a bounded per-mod queue (deltas coalesced, `dropped` counted).
routes.app.server_request: Q1 `app_server_request` event: observe a server-to-client request and its resolution; the native handler still answers it.
routes.approval: Q2 `approval` middleware: observe this decision point and tighten only (deny, or require a prompt where the host would skip); a mod can never approve.
routes.mod.event: An existing OMD event or replacement point (named in `via`) already exposes this surface; Q-series additions are named where they extend it.
routes.mod.api: An existing OMD registration API (named in `via`) is the public equivalent of this upstream extension seam.
routes.builtins.command: P6 plus Q10 builtin controls on a built-in slash command: `observe` its use, `invoke` it from a user context, `hide` it, or `replace` it with a mod command; `access` lists what is allowed.
routes.builtins.key: Q10 keymap overlay on a built-in keymap action: observe, rebind or unbind for the session (restored on disable), or invoke from a user context.
routes.terminal.list: 4ef `render` hook on component `list`: draw this native list view's rows and surroundings; keys, selection and persistence stay native.
routes.terminal.view: Q10 `view` event: observe this native view opening and closing; open it by invoking its command; hide it by hiding that command. `access` lists what is allowed.
routes.config.read: Q1 `config/read`: read the effective value and its origin (secrets redacted).
routes.config.write: Q1 `config/value/write` / `config/batchWrite` for this key, with a native confirmation naming the mod and value; also readable. `subkeys` limits writes to those sub-key patterns (`*` matches one segment).

exclusions.credentials: Authentication, login, logout, token refresh and credential setup stay kernel-only. Mods see opaque credential profiles through Q6 and never start or answer login flows.
exclusions.spending: Consumes paid credits or answers a billing prompt; only the user authorizes spending, in native UI.
exclusions.sandbox_bypass: Runs commands, processes or filesystem operations with a caller-chosen sandbox or outside the session permission profile. Mods use P1 `exec.run`, P2 `workspace.*` and Q5 `workspace.watch`, which enforce the session profile and protected paths.
exclusions.authority_decision: Answers or approves an approval, permission, elicitation, user-input or trust prompt, or rebinds its keys. Decisions stay with the user; mods observe and may only tighten through Q2.
exclusions.transcript_integrity: Appends raw model items to history outside a turn, which would let a mod forge assistant or tool evidence. Mods use `context`, `turn/steer` or queued user input instead.
exclusions.remote_publish: Publishes to, uploads to or pairs with a remote service (feedback upload, plugin sharing, remote control, credit nudges). Outside local host authority; live collaboration relays are not queued.
exclusions.realtime_media: Live audio sessions bind microphone and speaker devices and a separate realtime transport; speech tooling is not queued. Realtime notifications stay observable.
exclusions.execution_targets: Adds or selects a remote execution environment, which changes where commands run.
exclusions.host_lifecycle: Shuts down or suspends the host process; process lifecycle and `/omd` recovery stay native.
exclusions.protocol_internal: Connection handshake, subscription bookkeeping, attestation, clock or raw internal streams, not a user-facing surface. OMD's `model_request` and `response_stream` events expose the observed request and stream.
exclusions.deprecated: Deprecated upstream compatibility method; its replacement is routed.
exclusions.platform_windows: Windows sandbox setup; OMD targets macOS and Linux builds.
exclusions.authority_config: Sets sandbox, approvals, permissions, credentials, network or proxy access, command execution, provider endpoints, trust or data locations. Readable through `config.read`; never writable by mods, even with confirmation, except listed `subkeys` that only switch user-configured entries on or off.
exclusions.unmediated_tool_call: Calls an MCP tool outside a model turn, bypassing per-call approval and accounting. Mods register their own tools or spawn agents.
